After more than a decade of not adding touchscreens to its Mac laptop lineup, Apple is finally set to release its first MacBook with a touchscreen as early as October. The new machine will debut alongside the next-generation MacBook Pro refresh and may be named the MacBook Ultra.

Of course, rumours are still just rumours — but nearly all credible sources agree that the MacBook Pro will gain touch support later this year. Apple has even left behind some clues in macOS 27: Sidecar touch support, pull-to-refresh functionality, and slightly enlarged menu bar items.

As a 13-inch MacBook Air user, that last point is particularly annoying to me, because things that used to fit on the left side of the notch are now starting to overflow.

You might say these are just coincidences, but it really does look like that's exactly what's happening. Setting that aside, here's what the first MacBook with a touchscreen is expected to offer.

OLED, Dynamic Island

On the display front, the refreshed MacBook Pro will feature a Tandem OLED screen, with specifications similar to the iPad Pro — which is frequently hailed as one of the best mobile displays on the market. Tandem OLED uses a dual-layer stacked OLED panel design, delivering richer colours, stronger contrast, and higher brightness.

Reports suggest the new machine will adopt the Dynamic Island, albeit slightly smaller than the one on iPhones. However, the new machine will not support Face ID.

Software Optimisations

According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple will add a number of special optimisations to the first touchscreen MacBook Pro beyond what's already been seen in macOS 27 betas:

"For example, if a user touches a button or control, a new type of menu will pop up around their fingers, offering options more relevant to touch operation. The software will also display the most appropriate set of controls based on the user's past interaction habits. If someone taps an item on the menu bar at the top of the screen, that set of controls will also be enlarged, making it easier to select with a finger."

M5 Pro and M5 Max Chips

Although earlier reports had indicated that the refreshed MacBook Pro would be the first to feature M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, Apple has now decided to skip the release of these two chips and accelerate development of the M7. In other words, the first batch of 2nm-process chips will not be used in the refreshed MacBook Pro — the new machine will stick with the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

There won't be an entry-level model for now either, though rumours suggest Apple may launch an entry-level refreshed MacBook Pro with an M7 chip as early as next spring.

Slightly Thinner Body

One of the design rumours about the new MacBook Pro is that it will be slightly thinner and lighter — though the exact extent of the difference remains unclear. The previous-generation MacBook Pro looked and felt quite chunky, so if this generation could improve in that area, it would likely be well received — as long as it doesn't sacrifice thermal performance in the name of slimming down.

Summary

Overall, the first MacBook Pro with a touchscreen looks set to be an exciting upgrade. Since Apple raised prices earlier due to a memory shortage, the new machine's pricing will also go up — the 14-inch model is expected to start at US$2,499, while the 16-inch will be around US$3,099.

Are you looking forward to a touchscreen MacBook? Will you grab one at launch, or wait a bit for the cheaper 14-inch entry-level model? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
